lines.li: [us] What's {TOWN} like these days?
[them,their:tribal] A few longhouses and a drying rack, and a fire that hasn't gone out since we lit it.
[them,their:medieval] A dozen roofs, a common well, and a fence the goats have already got through.
[them,their:industrial] A water pump, a fence line, and houses that still smell of new timber.
[them,their:spacer] A few sealed domes, a hydroponics shed and a weather mast that keeps falling over.
[them] Small and new, and every roof on it put up by our own hands.
[us] It sounds like home.
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] It will be, if we get through the year.
[them] It's getting there, one roof at a time.
[them,their:tribal] Every quarrel at the new hearth comes to my fire, and most are about who hunts where.
[them,their:hightech] Every dispute at {TOWN} lands on my desk, and most are about water rights.
[them] Every quarrel at {TOWN} comes to my door, and most of them are about fences.
[us] Is it hard, leading them?
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] Easier, knowing your colony is close.
[them] Harder than founding it, and that was hard enough.
[them] I led the families out to {TOWN}, and some nights I still wonder if it was wise.
[us] Was it?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Ask me after the next harvest.
[them] The fields say so, and I'm learning to trust the fields.
[them] Winter at {TOWN} means three families to a house and the woodpile watched like gold.
[us] Do you have enough to eat?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Not quite, but we're careful with it.
[them] Enough, if the snow doesn't stay too long.
[them] We're breaking new ground at {TOWN} this spring, a field further out than the last.
[us] Is the land good?
[them,home:desert] Thin, but it takes water well enough.
[them,home:forest] Good, once the stumps are out, and the stumps are never all out.
[them,home:cold] Short-seasoned, so we plant fast and pray the frost is late.
[them] Better than we hoped, and we hoped for a lot.
[them] Every hand at {TOWN} is in the fields this time of year, even the children's.
[us] Who keeps watch?
[them] The old ones, and the dogs, and we trust your colony for the rest.
[them] My children talk about {TOWN} as if it had always been there.
[us] That's how it should be.
[them] I hope so, it's a lot to put on a few houses.
[them] {TOWN} is still young enough that we all know who built which wall.
[us] And who built yours?
[them] I did, and it's the straightest one there.
[them] {TOWN} has outgrown its first fence, and we've had to move it out.
[us] That's good news.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say a hearth that grows is a hearth the spirits like.
[them] It is, the fields have been good to us.
[them] We heard raiders came at your walls, and {TOWN} was sick with worry.
[us] We held.
[them] Good, because if you fall, we're next.
[them] With our people at war, {TOWN} feels very small and very far out.
[us] You're under our protection.
[them] That's what we keep telling each other at night.
[them] You walked beside our carts to {TOWN}, I'd know you anywhere.
[us] A long road, that one.
[them] The children still play at that walk, and one of them always has to be you.
[us] I hope they make me taller.
[them] Taller and braver, you should hear them.
[them] Did our carter bring you what we sent from the harvest?
[us] It came, thank you.
[them,their:tribal] Good, the first of the harvest belongs to those who walked us there.
[them] Good, it isn't much, but it's the first of what the land gave us.
[them] What your colony sent us in the hard season got {TOWN} through it.
[us] We were glad to.
[them,their:tribal] The elders cut a mark on the lodge post for it, so the children will ask.
[them] We haven't forgotten it, and we don't mean to.
[them] My people still speak of the help you sent to {DEEDNAME} in a hard season.
[us] They'd have done the same.
[them] Maybe, but you were the ones near enough to do it.
[them] Our hamlet asked your colony for help in a hard season, and got nothing.
[us] We couldn't spare it then.
[them] So you said.
[them] {WRONGNAME} turned to you in a hard season, and you turned away.
[us] It wasn't an easy choice.
[them] {TOWN} pays its way with the harvest, so don't think we're beholden.
[us] We never said you were.
[them] Being under your protection doesn't put us under your feet.
[us] Then stop standing under them.
[us,tribal] The clan's spear is over {TOWN}, for as long as we stand.
[us,medieval] {TOWN} has our protection, and we keep our word.
[us,spacer] {TOWN} is under our charter of protection, that hasn't changed.
[us] {TOWN} has our guarantee, for whatever comes.
[them] We know, and the families there sleep better for it.
[them] Our people have troubles of their own just now, so {TOWN} looks to you more than to them.
[us] We know.
[them] We try not to make a habit of it.
[them] An outpost of the Empire under a colony's protection is not a thing the court is used to.
[us] And you?
[them] I am getting used to it, one season at a time.
[them] I swore for every family at {TOWN}, and some of them still ask me what it means.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them,their:tribal] That when trouble comes to either fire, the other comes running.
[them] That if trouble comes, we stand with your colony and it stands with us.
[us] Do your people mind the oath?
[them,their:tribal] The gifts went into the river and the river took them, so it is done.
[them,their:medieval] It was sworn before witnesses, and that settles it for anyone at {TOWN}.
[them,their:industrial] It's signed and filed, and our people respect a signature.
[them,their:spacer] The charter is registered, which is about as binding as anything gets out here.
[them] Some do, but most of us sleep easier for it.
[them] {TOWN} isn't {HAMLETWORD} anymore, our people count it a proper town now.
[us] We heard.
[them] It still looks to your colony first, that hasn't changed.
[them,their:tribal] Our young hunters talk of {HAMLET} as if it were the best ground in the world.
[them] The young ones at home talk about {HAMLET} as if it were the edge of the world.
[us] It's not so far.
[them] Far enough, when you're seventeen and want a roof of your own.
[them] Families I've known all my life went out to {HAMLET} under your protection.
[us] They're doing all right.
[them] So they say, and they'd tell me if they weren't, I think.
[them] Settlers like those at {HAMLET} always need nails and needles.
[us] Are you headed there?
[them] After you, if you leave me anything to sell.
[them] A hamlet of {HAMLETPEOPLE} under your protection, so your colony keeps vassals now.
[us] It's a hamlet, not a fief.
[them] Every fief I know of began as somebody's hamlet.
[them] The trails say {HAMLETPEOPLE} lit a fire at {HAMLET}, under your spears.
[us] We walked them there.
[them] Then their fire is partly yours, and so is its smoke.
